note: One order-independent rule set. It was seven files applied in a fixed order, where a later file's wider matchers were survived rather than corrected -- eight of those ninety rules are unsound on their own, and would mislabel 8077 positions if the file boundaries were removed. One of them, `attention.q_b_proj <- 'cublasLt::splitKreduce_kernel'`, never once claims a position that carries its operation: it was only ever right because an earlier file had already taken the ones it would have got wrong. So the labels were a property of how the filenames sorted, and nothing checked it. Matchers here were narrowed until no position is claimed by two rules with different operations. Two checks hold the property: `subsumptions` proves order-dependence from the rule file alone and runs in `alignment-campaign check`; `disagreements` observes it against a real capture at the fixpoint and runs in `alignment-campaign label`. Both are in `alignment/labeling/rules.py`.
merged_from_note: These seven files no longer exist in the pack; they are named because `merged_sources` records where each came from. The chain as applied is kept at logs/20260826_0_glm52_b200_ep4_workload_matrix_realign/labeling_rules/.
reason: retired split routing/gate_up/down/finalize slots; replaced by aggregate fused_moe rule
provenance: Derived from the layered chain at logs/20260826_0_glm52_b200_ep4_workload_matrix_realign/labeling_rules/, which produced the accepted cases 01-08. Every rule keeps its `source_experiment`, which is what the seven filenames used to carry. The other candidate, the single-file chain in logs/20260827_1_.../labeling_rules.json, reproduces cases 09-15 exactly but leaves 18% of batch-0 kernel positions unmapped.

reproduction.note: Measured by applying this rule set to a fresh parse of each accepted case's kernel_sequences.json and comparing against that case's accepted kernel_sequences_labeled.json, position by position in walk order. Written by the migration, not by hand.
reproduction.order_dependence_note: The rule list is shuffled and re-applied to a fixpoint; this counts the positions whose (status, operation) moved. Zero means the labels are a property of the rules rather than of their order in the file.
reproduction.ledger_note: Three unlike things the old single `positions_differing_from_accepted` added together. `wrong` is the only defect: a position both label and the accepted document map, to different operations. `lost` is narrower coverage, `gained` is wider -- the accepted document leaves those positions unmapped. The 1058 this field used to record was entirely `gained`, so it never counted a mistake.
reproduction.duration_note: Position counts are the wrong currency for the coverage trade: the lost positions are GEMMs and their split-K reduces, the gained ones are mostly elementwise. `mapping.coverage.measured_duration_fraction` is what the acceptance gate reads, so the same ledger is given in the milliseconds the analyzer's kernel inventory records for those launches.
